look_here_first: Bushy upright amaranth with the easiest character in the genus: a pair of sharp spines at nearly every leaf node.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays-local source, but current Kew distribution treats Texas as introduced; retained as a comparison learner.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Installed for visual learning; only current native-range evidence should feed native metrics.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Amaranthaceae/Amaranthus: alternate petiolate leaves and dense clusters of tiny unisexual flowers. Habit, plant sex, hairiness, nodal spines, cluster position, bract/tepal form, and fruit dehiscence are high-value characters.
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Paired nodal spines make it nearly immediate. None of the other B114 species routinely has this feature.
